headline: Binance reopens HYPE and APT withdrawals after its $6.3B hack, MEXC says it is operating normally after a US Treasury cut-off order, and bitcoin heads into its weekly close after a $1.28B ETF outflow week.

stories.title: Binance reopens HYPE and APT withdrawals as hack clean-up continues
stories.summary: Binance restored withdrawals for Hyperliquid (HYPE) and Aptos (APT) on 8 November, the latest step in reopening after its $6.3B hack. It aims to reopen the rest of its six named coins by the end of next week. That is a target, not a fixed date.
points: Earlier phases reopened BTC plus 15 networks on 1 Nov and stablecoins and tokens such as LINK, SHIB and ONDO on 3 Nov, per crypto.news.
INJ, Plasma (XPL), NEAR and LTC were also on Binance's list of six coins to reopen by the end of next week, per CoinStats.
Sources differ on how much has been replaced: about 95% per crypto.news on 8 Nov, 98% per CoinStats citing Binance's 4 Nov update.
The hack's size is given as $6.3B by crypto.news; about $2.85B has been frozen or intercepted, per crypto.news.
Binance has committed to refill its SAFU emergency fund to about $1B, per crypto.news.

sources.label: crypto.news: Binance restores HYPE and APT withdrawals

stories.title: MEXC says it is operating normally after the US Treasury moves to cut it off
stories.summary: The Treasury's financial-crimes unit, FinCEN, ordered US financial institutions to stop processing transfers involving MEXC Global, alleging at least $16 billion in illicit flows. MEXC says user assets are secure and it is reviewing the order. The ban starts 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register, and that date is not yet set.
points: FinCEN alleges at least $16B in illicit transactions, per FinCEN.
That includes about $1B with more than 40 Iranian exchanges, per crypto.news.
Nearly $1.5B is tied to evading Russian sanctions, per 24/7 Wall St.
This is not an asset freeze: US users could see failed bank transfers once the order is in force, per 24/7 Wall St.
MEXC has started an independent review of its anti-money-laundering controls, per crypto.news.

stories.title: Bitcoin heads for a fifth losing week after $1.28B left US bitcoin funds
stories.summary: Investors pulled a net $1.28 billion from US spot bitcoin ETFs in the week of 2-6 November, per crypto.news. Bitcoin has had four losing weeks in a row; a weekly close tonight below the week's open would make it five.
points: BlackRock's IBIT lost $1.21B over the week, while Fidelity's FBTC took in $93.1M, per crypto.news citing Farside.
Ether ETFs lost $365.2M over the same week, with BlackRock's ETHA down $345.9M, per crypto.news.
The week's open is $78,232 per CryptoTicker and $78,354 per crypto.news; the week's low was $74,888 per crypto.news and $74,722 per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: SEC opens trading in third-party tokenized US stocks
briefs.summary: A temporary SEC order lets some venues trade tokenized US shares made by third parties; issuers get 30 days to object, and OKX is seeking approval for 63 stocks, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Kalshi midterm markets top $2.5B
briefs.summary: Kalshi says its 2026 midterm markets traded more than $2.5B, about double 2024's $1.3B, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Travel-rule plan withdrawal takes effect 9 Nov
briefs.summary: The withdrawal of the proposal to cut the travel-rule threshold from $3,000 to $250 takes effect 9 Nov, per crypto.news.
